content.text:
I reviewed `0.html` and made no changes: I couldn't find an edit that would make it better rather than just different.

This is from reading the code only. I tried to render it in headless Chrome to check the screen and print output, but this session denied those commands, so nothing was visually verified.

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Document basics | Doctype, `lang`, charset, viewport, title and description are all present. |
| Centering | The grid on `body` with a `100vh` → `100dvh` fallback handles mobile browser toolbars. |
| Sizing | `min(25rem, 100vmin - 2rem)` keeps the circle on screen in any orientation and scales with the user's font size. |
| Edge rendering | `overflow: visible` stops the antialiased edge being clipped, since the circle exactly fills its viewBox. |
| Dark mode | The `color-scheme` meta tag plus `fill: currentColor` adapts with no extra rules, and the favicon adapts too. |
| High-contrast mode | `currentColor` resolves to the system text colour, so the circle stays visible. |
| Accessibility | `role="img"` with `aria-label` inside the `<h1>` inside `<main>` gives the page a named heading and a landmark. |
| Print | Forcing the fill to `#000` is a harmless safeguard. |

One thing I would check in a browser is print preview: `min-height: 100vh` on `body` can sometimes spill onto a blank second page. If it does, adding `body { min-height: 0; }` inside the existing `@media print` block fixes it, at the cost of vertical centering on paper. I left it alone because I couldn't confirm the problem exists.

If you had a specific direction in mind, such as animation, interactivity, a different look or a smaller file, tell me which and I'll make the change.
